approaches.role-words-only:
"""Role words refused, any other name accepted (approach role-words-only)."""
import re

DOOR = re.compile(r"^unassigned — (?P<who>.+?) by (?P<when>.+)$")
ROLE = re.compile(r"\b(?:lead|owner|leadership|team|head|manager|director|partners?)\b", re.I)


def apply(case):
    pack = case["pack"]
    doors = []
    for index, row in enumerate(pack.get("ownership") or []):
        owner = str(row.get("owner") or "").strip()
        match = DOOR.match(owner)
        if not match:
            continue
        who = re.sub(r"\s+must assign it$", "", match.group("who").strip())
        if ROLE.search(who):
            raise ValueError(f"tactical_roadmap_door_assigner_unnamed: ownership[{index}] ({row.get('element')}) names a role {who!r}")
        doors.append(f"- **Assign the {row.get('element')} owner** — {owner[len('unassigned — '):]}")
    return {"refusal": None, "rendered": "\n".join(doors), "pack": pack}

activation_cards.name: Public Identity Cleanup
activation_cards.insight: A proof-led AI story fails if buyer-facing records conflict before the proof is seen.
activation_cards.idea: Clean The B Team's public identity around The Stop Line before launch so the market sees one consistent proof-first story; any cleaned public record is live, unpromoted, until the Launch moment in Month 4.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Buyers, partners and media encounter consistent public records before being asked to evaluate The Stop Line.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The launch has no unresolved public-profile conflicts undermining credibility.
activation_cards.targets: Public website, LinkedIn profiles, sales decks, media boilerplate and buyer-facing descriptions read in Month 1; conflicts logged and resolved before Month 4.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, partners, media and senior Sofia talent.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Proof comes before promotion.
activation_cards.kpi: Public-profile consistency rate measured as percentage of identified buyer-facing records passing the Public Identity Cleanup Checklist; unresolved conflict count; approved boilerplate adoption rate.

activation_cards.name: Proof Library Lock
activation_cards.insight: The Stop Line can only be ownable if every AI claim shows approved proof, a senior owner and a stated limit.
activation_cards.idea: Lock the proof library behind The Stop Line before promotion, with every claim labelled as named reference, verifiable anonymous reference, technical artifact or internal demo.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Internal reviewers read each claim against its proof type, owner and stop-line limit before it can enter public use.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The year starts from an approved proof base instead of a list of AI claims.
activation_cards.targets: All public AI claims, proof labels, senior-owner fields and stated limits read in Month 1; launch claims approved before Month 4.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, partners and sales users.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Every public AI claim must connect to approved proof.
activation_cards.kpi: Percentage of launch AI claims linked to approved proof; percentage of proof entries passing the Proof Library Lock Checklist; number of claims rejected or narrowed before publication.

activation_cards.name: Key-Message Table
activation_cards.insight: A distributed launch needs one approved source of message truth or local teams will stretch the claim.
activation_cards.idea: Produce the Key-Message Table for The Stop Line and Signed by Humans as the approved training source for audiences, proof points and do-not-say lines.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Spokespeople, sales and partners read one approved message table before creating launch or follow-up material.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: Every tactic uses the same proof-first restraint language.
activation_cards.targets: Audience messages, proof points, do-not-say lines and approval owners read in Month 1; table used from Month 1 through Month 12.
activation_cards.audience: Internal spokespeople, sales users, partners and local market leads.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Clear limits make the AI story easier to trust.
activation_cards.kpi: Message-table completion rate; percentage of assets passing the Key-Message Table Alignment Rubric on audience fit, proof trace, claim limit and do-not-say compliance; approved-answer reuse rate.

activation_cards.name: The Stop Line Proof Page
activation_cards.insight: Buyers do not need a bigger AI promise; they need to see what is proved, who owns it and where the system stops.
activation_cards.idea: Create one owned page for The Stop Line that is live, unpromoted, until the Launch moment in Month 4, showing each approved claim with proof type, senior owner and stated limit.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Visitors can inspect the proof behind the claim before they are asked to book a meeting or accept the AI story.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The B Team has a public proof base that paid, earned, shared and sales activity can all point to.
activation_cards.targets: Proof page read internally in Month 2 and published live, unpromoted, from Month 2 until launch promotion in Month 4; all launch claims checked before Month 4.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, partners and senior Sofia talent.
activation_cards.message_pillar: The Stop Line makes restraint visible.
activation_cards.kpi: Proof-page visits; time on page; qualified meeting clicks; percentage of public AI claims linked to approved proof; page quality scored on a 1-5 Stop Line Proof Page Checklist covering proof type, senior owner, limit and buyer clarity.

activation_cards.name: Fact Sheet and Backgrounder
activation_cards.insight: Media, partners and technical buyers need the approval route and claim limits in a form they can cite safely.
activation_cards.idea: Build the fact sheet and backgrounder explaining The Stop Line, Signed by Humans, proof types, senior sign-off and claim boundaries.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Readers get a compact reference that answers what is proved, who approved it and what is not being claimed.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: Earned, partner and sales conversations stay inside the approved proof boundary.
activation_cards.targets: Fact sheet and backgrounder read in Month 2; used from Month 4 through Month 12 for launch, partner and earned activity.
activation_cards.audience: Journalists, analysts, partners, enterprise buyers and sales users.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Senior people still own the outcome.
activation_cards.kpi: Approval-route accuracy rate; percentage of backgrounder sections passing the Fact Sheet Accuracy Checklist; proof citations used in briefings; media-question answer reuse.

activation_cards.name: Owner Control Message Test
activation_cards.insight: Owners may value control and visibility more than AI capability, but that remains a hypothesis until owners compare the messages.
activation_cards.idea: Test a control-led message against an AI-capability message, both anchored in The Stop Line.
activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Owners react to plain-language options showing visibility, ownership and early risk detection without being asked to become technical buyers.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: The B Team learns whether control should lead owner-facing communication before scaling the message.
activation_cards.targets: Owner test responses read in Month 3; preference, comprehension, trust and meeting-intent evidence reviewed before Month 4 launch language is promoted.
activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, led by Elena.
activation_cards.message_pillar: Owners get control without becoming technical.
activation_cards.kpi: Preference split; comprehension score on a 1-5 owner-clarity scale; trust lift; meeting intent; qualitative reasons coded against the Owner Control Message Test Rubric.

activation_cards.name: Spokesperson Training and Q&A

activation_cards.engagement_mechanic: Spokespeople rehearse buyer, partner and media questions and learn the approved escalation route.
activation_cards.desired_outcome: Launch answers stay consistent, specific and proof-led.
activation_cards.targets: Spokesperson materials, Q&A and 30-second pitch read in Month 3; every launch spokesperson trained before Month 4.
activation_cards.audience: Founders, senior leaders, sales users and market spokespeople.
activation_cards.message_pillar: If evidence is missing, the message narrows.
activation_cards.kpi: Training completion rate; answer quality scored on a 1-5 Spokesperson Stop Line Rubric for proof trace, owner naming, limit clarity and escalation discipline; number of unapproved claims corrected before launch.

activation_cards.audience: Owners of midsize businesses, technical buyers, partners, journalists and senior Sofia talent.
activation_cards.message_pillar: The B Team makes AI credible by showing The Stop Line before it promotes the AI claim.
activation_cards.kpi: Proof-page visits; earned coverage quality scored on a 1-5 Launch Coverage Quality Rubric for proof citation, claim accuracy and stop-line mention; qualified meeting clicks; launch-asset approval pass rate.
